faculty: Faculty of Science and Agriculture, Business and Law
description: Accounting is at the centre of business and finance - from tracking the flow of money to analysing financial activities. The skills you develop through the Bachelor of Accounting are fundamental to making strategic business decisions and helping people stay in control of their money. Our Bachelor of Accounting is a premier undergraduate degree accredited with CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CA ANZ). Upon completion of the core units you will meet the entry requirements for these professional accounting bodies. You will develop specialised knowledge of the accounting discipline, including technical skills and critical thinking, as well as the skills to collect, measure, and communicate financial information in a range of situations. This degree comprises a set of core units in accounting, auditing, information systems, economics, finance, business, statistics, and law.In addition to the core, there are optional majors in Advanced Accounting, Agribusiness, Finance, Business Analysis and Transformation. As an alternative to these majors, the Bachelor of Accounting allows you to choose elective units from other disciplines across the University or through specialised minors. You might choose a set of units that will equip you for a career in a particular industry. If your aim is to become an accountant: in the film industry, choose screen or media studies units; in forensic accounting, accounting systems design, or auditing IT systems, choose from the computer science suite of units; with broader business skills, you can undertake management, marketing, human resource management or other units of your choice. The Bachelor of Accounting gives you the flexibility to take your accounting qualification in the specific direction you choose. Trimester 3 provides the opportunity to 'fast track' your degree and complete the Bachelor of Accounting in two years full time or four years part time if you choose elective units (rather than an additional major).Choose this path if you want to complete your degree as soon as possible. If opportunities to work overseas arise while you are studying, UNE provides the flexibility you need to continue your studies. With extensive experience offering accounting to students online, you can be confident of the quality of teaching and support wherever you are located. You can also study accounting in the Bachelor of Business .
duration: 3 Years Full-time; Up to 10 years Part-time

faculty: Faculty of Science and Agriculture, Business and Law
description: This double degree provides students with the opportunity to combine the study of an accredited law program with the study of an accredited accounting program. The study of the combined program gives students an in-depth understanding of the intersection between law and accounting, thereby enabling entry into a variety of career opportunities beyond those available to law or accounting graduates individually. Accounting component : Accounting is at the centre of business and finance, from tracking the flow of money to analysing financial activities. The skills students develop through the Bachelor of Accounting are fundamental to making strategic business decisions and helping people stay in control of their money. Within the Bachelor of Accounting, students develop specialised knowledge of the accounting discipline, including technical skills and critical thinking skills, as well as the skills to collect, measure, and communicate financial information in a range of situations. The UNE Bachelor of Accounting is a premier undergraduate degree accredited with CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CA ANZ). Upon completion of the core units graduates will meet the entry requirements for these professional accounting bodies. Law component : The Bachelor of Laws provides a strong foundation in Law, and there are a range of employment options from which graduates may choose. Graduates who wish to be admitted to practice as a solicitor, barrister or legal practitioner anywhere in Australia will also have to undertake a course of practical legal training (PLT). This can consist of approximately half a year's full-time training, undertaken internally or externally, or of equivalent part-time training. In some jurisdictions, it may be possible to do articles of clerkship instead. Because the system adopted varies from jurisdiction to jurisdiction, enquiries should be made to the admission authority in the state or territory in which you intend to practice; this is usually a committee of the Supreme Court of that State or Territory or a special body set up to administer admissions to the legal profession. Additional information can be found on the School of Law page . Students who complete the Honours Pathway may be awarded the Bachelor of Laws with Honours. To be admitted to the Bachelor of Laws Honours stream, candidates must have completed 72 credit points of law units at UNE with a grade point average (GPA) of 5.5 or better. The University of New England delivers a flexible approach to the study of law. UNE boasts one of Australia's largest law schools outside a capital city, as well as being an early adopter of innovative technology in the delivery of its law programs

faculty: Faculty of Science and Agriculture, Business and Law
description: The Bachelor of Agribusiness at UNE prepares graduates to address the most pressing challenges and opportunities in the global food and agribusiness sector. The program builds the skills and knowledge needed to tackle critical issues such as food safety and security, climate change, sustainability, and the increasing globalisation and integration of agricultural and food networks. With a strong foundation in business and economics, students are equipped to analyse complex problems and drive innovation across the agribusiness value chain. The Bachelor of Agribusiness is accredited by the European Foundation for Management Development (EFMD) under EFMD Program Accreditation. This accreditation is a globally recognised process and signifies a commitment to excellence in curriculum design, teaching methods, student assessment, and quality assurance processes. Studies may be tailored to individual interests and career goals by selecting from a range of majors, including Business, Agricultural Production, Agricultural and Natural Resource Economics, Marketing and Management, and Finance. Those with an entrepreneurial mindset are able to complement their studies with a minor in Entrepreneurship and Innovation, gaining tools to develop new ventures and creative solutions for the agribusiness sector. Opportunities exist to gain real-world skills through optional practical work experience, as well as to broaden horizons with overseas study tours and exchange programs that add extra value to the degree. UNE agribusiness graduates enjoy excellent employment prospects, with an average of over 90% securing employment soon after graduation with competitive starting salaries. With its industry relevance, practical skill development, and global outlook, the Bachelor of Agribusiness equips graduates to make a meaningful impact in a rapidly evolving industry—locally, nationally, and globally.
duration: 3 Years Full-time; Up to 10 years Part-time

courseName: Bachelor of Agricultural and Resource Economics
description: This course is not offered in 2026. Demand for agricultural business professionals continues to grow. The Bachelor of Agricultural and Resource Economics at UNE is the longest running agricultural and resource economics degree in Australia. Through the study of agricultural and resource economics you will gain an understanding of the key challenges and trade-offs confronting business, government and the community at large. You will develop the knowledge, skills and attributes required for high level problem solving and economic decision making across a diverse range of agricultural and natural resource issues such as food safety and security, natural resource depletion, climate change, sustainability and increasing globalisation and integration of agricultural and food networks. Core units include microeconomics and macroeconomics, farm and resource management, rural finance and risk management, environmental and natural resource economics, international trade and business, and economic analysis of chains and networks. This degree is taught with a global perspective to ensure you understand the current challenging issues across the economic, environmental, social and political environments.You will also develop an understanding of social responsibility in relation to agricultural and business practices, and an appreciation of the importance of the environment and sustainability. The degree gives students the flexibility to choose between a coursework only option and an embedded Honours program in which you undertake a supervised program of reading and research involving the preparation of a dissertation that reports on a particular investigation of an area of economic enquiry. Opportunities also exist to undertake practical work experience and to participate in overseas study tours and study exchange programs that value add to the degree.

description: This degree produces graduates with skills in increasing demand in the rural sector. A practically orientated degree, students are provided with the tools necessary to understand the implications of land use and management change on agricultural productivity. Once armed with the basic knowledge to understand sustainable agricultural systems, graduates are able to continue on to further study in specific areas of interest. This degree suits students who are more interested in the productive management of agricultural landscapes in contrast to the scientific, agricultural systems focus of other agricultural based degree programs offered at UNE. The major completed will appear on the academic record and testamur. Students have ready access to eight University properties covering 3,655 hectares, located on and close to campus including the SMART Farms and Tullimba Research Feedlot. Graduates are eligible for membership of the AG Institute Australia. Fully credited exchange programs of one trimester are in place with international universities. Q Fever: It is a condition that all students enrolled in this course must be vaccinated against Q Fever (unless initial skin test indicates pre-existing immunity). This must be completed as soon as possible and by no later than the end of the first trimester of study. Q Fever screening and vaccination can be arranged through the University Medical Centre, or through your own GP. The cost of the vaccination program is separate to tuition fees.

description: Our Bachelor of Business will help you navigate the world of business across a range of industries and occupations. You will develop skills in creative thinking and critical analysis, communication and business decision making. You will be able to develop and lead ethical, social and environmental solutions to meet business challenges. Alternatively undertake OSSE300 our Overseas Study Experience unit and have the opportunity to travel overseas with fellow students on a guided tour of large multi-national businesses in Asia. Most students who decide to complete only one major can choose a further eight (8) units from any discipline across the university in order to truly broaden the learning experience. The Business School operates its own Smart Region Incubator which provides a supportive community for start-ups in the region. In the Cybersecurity major, students learn topics such as cryptography, cloud security, cybersecurity risk management, and ethical hacking. In the Data Science major, students learn topics that are of particular relevance to applying computing to science. In the Software Development major, students study topics such as advanced features of modern programming languages, functional programming, programming parallel and distributed systems, development for the modern web, and interaction design. description: The Bachelor of Counselling at UNE is informed and underpinned by Humanistic and Existential counselling philosophies which deal with questions of meaning and freedom, grapple with what it means to be human and emphasise the value of individual and collective agency. Humanistic counselling approaches offer a way of 'being' in the world and a focus on the person rather than the symptoms. Humanistic approaches require a commitment on the part of the counsellor to self-knowledge and, at the same time, to the understanding that this self-knowledge is never fully attained. This requires a degree of emotional and psychological agility. Your success in this award will be strongly linked to your willingness to engage in supported, self-directed and reflexive learning; to connect with others, and to explore what emerges during these connections. As part of its growth-promoting focus, the Bachelor of Counselling will assist you to develop qualities of genuineness, acceptance, caring, compassion, and accurate empathic understanding; to acquire a strong foundation in counselling theory and practice; and to be well-equipped for future work as a registered counsellor with a diverse clientele from a variety of cultural backgrounds Combining online study with mandatory intensive schools, this course is ideally suited to individuals wishing to gain an industry-recognised qualification whilst continuing to meet their work and family commitments. description: The University of New England offers a flexible approach to the study of law. Studying law in conjunction with another discipline gives you the potential to take an interdisciplinary approach in both your studies and in your future employment. Law component: The Bachelor of Laws is accredited by the Legal Profession Admission Board of NSW for admission as a legal practitioner in NSW and mutual recognition legislation extends admission to other Australian jurisdictions. After completion of academic qualifications there are a range of employment options from which to choose. Graduates who wish to be admitted to practice as a solicitor, barrister or legal practitioner anywhere in Australia will also have to undertake a course of practical legal training (PLT). This can consist of approximately half a year's full-time training, undertaken internally or externally, or of equivalent part-time training. In some jurisdictions, it may be possible to do articles of clerkship instead. Because the system adopted varies from jurisdiction to jurisdiction, enquiries should be made to the admission authority in the state or territory in which you intend to practice: this is usually a committee of the Supreme Court of that State or Territory or a special body set up to administer admissions to the legal profession. Additional information can be found on the School of Law page. Students who complete the Honours Pathway may be awarded the degree of Bachelor of Laws with Honours. courseName: Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood Education and Care)
description: The Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood Education and Care) has been accredited by the Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority (ACECQA), and leads to opportunities to work in a range of Early Childhood organisations. It has been designed to qualify graduates as four-year trained Early Childhood Teachers. This degree focuses on birth to five-years and provides students with diverse experiences to study, learn and reflect on the teaching and learning of young children. Students enter the Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood Education and Care) via two different pathways. Pathway 1 is for those students who meet admission requirements to enter at the third or fourth year level of study. Their previous qualifications and work experience are recognised in place of the first two years of the degree as block 'advanced standing' (also known as 'recognised prior learning'). Such students then complete one or two years of university study. Pathway 2 is for those students who are school leavers and for those students who do not have any ECE qualifications. Differing rules apply to the two pathways. How your admission rule affects the duration and structure of your course is explained in the dot points below. Rule A students Receive credit for the first two years of study and start directly in the third year. Complete 80 days of professional experience (practicum).† Choose the order in which you complete the major topics (called ‘clusters’). Each cluster is made up of one introductory unit and one follow-up unit. Rule B students Receive credit for the first three years of study and start directly in fourth year. Complete 45 days of professional experience (practicum).† Skip the introductory units, and complete most units in the order of your choice, subject to some requirements. Rule C students In the first 2 years of your course, complete foundational units, literacy and numeracy units, and 4 elective units. In the final 2 years of your course, complete 80 days of professional experience (practicum)† and your major topics (called ‘clusters’). Each cluster is made up of one introductory unit and one advanced unit. Placement Notes: All Professional Experience must be completed in ACECQA-approved centre-based settings that meets the National Quality Standard. Most professional experience placements in the third and fourth years of the course can be completed in the early learning service where you work (subject to some requirements). A few field experience days are tied to assignments to create a richer experience linking theory to practice. † Please note: Prospective students from states other than NSW should seek advice from their state and territory accrediting bodies regarding registration requirements as an Early Childhood Teacher in that state or territory. The Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood Education and Care) is not recognised for teaching in public primary schools. Commencement in Trimester 3 is only available to candidates admitted under Rule A or Rule C. This course is accredited with the Australian Children’s Education & Care Quality Authority (ACECQA) and is undergoing a change request to consolidate sixteen 3-credit point Early Childhood Education units into eight 6-credit point units. As such the course is subject to change prior to commencement in 2026.

faculty: Faculty of Science and Agriculture, Business and Law
description: The Bachelor of Environmental Science is a unique undergraduate program directly integrated to the protection and conservation of our regional, rural and national environment. It provides graduates with a strong scientific understanding of local to global environmental issues and their management. The program offers a wide range of flexible and personal learning opportunities to develop advanced scientific knowledge and field and laboratory skills related to ecological conservation, air, land, water, plant and wildlife management and protection. Students will engage and work with environmental practitioners, industry and regulators to solve the problems of today with innovative solutions whilst gaining the core attributes to be job ready in a wide range of careers. Local and international field trips give valuable hands on experience. The Bachelor of Environmental Science provides opportunity for specialisation or majors in applied management, conservation and ecology, natural resources, people and environment, and vegetation and landscapes. The program allows a wide choice of minors in botany, geoscience, zoology, soils, spatial science, global environments, water science, data science and modelling, and science communication. An Honours year is available to students with a GPA of 5.5 or better, or a credit average in at least 24 credit points at 300-level in environmental science units. description: The Bachelor of Exercise and Sports Science at UNE is a multidisciplinary program that develops a comprehensive understanding of the scientific and applied aspects of sport, exercise and health. The course includes core studies in human structure, function and behaviour before further study on the acute and chronic physiological and psychological responses to exercise. Analytical, technical and professional skills are developed in the areas of movement analysis, health and fitness assessment and exercise training for health and performance. Students complete 140 hours of workplace experience in their final trimester of study to practice these skills. Graduates are recognised for their expertise in the design and implementation of exercise interventions to prevent disease and improve health and wellbeing across healthy and sporting populations. For more information regarding the course or the process, please see the ESSA website here. Graduates who apply for initial accreditation with ESSA must demonstrate English language competence. description: This innovative degree provides the opportunity to study a geology degree that incorporates the fundamental core principals of geology coupled with teaching of both modern GIS and traditional mapping techniques. The New England Orogen is a great natural laboratory, and we have a diverse array of spectacular geology all easily accessible in our 'backyard'. description: The Bachelor of Health with Honours offers a dynamic blend of theoretical and practical learning, with the opportunity to work with industry partners and receive guidance from experienced supervisors. In the health sector, research plays a critical role in identifying gaps in service delivery, evaluating program effectiveness, and developing evidence-based policies and interventions. faculty: Faculty of Science and Agriculture, Business and Law
description: Information technology (IT) and computing increasingly define how the world operates. Software permeates every area of modern living, from the smallest personal device to automating entire industries. IT professionals are responsible for designing the software that runs so much of our lives, and for creating systems that handle and analyse incredible amounts of data. The Bachelor of Information Technology provides a versatile foundation in the field of information technology. It is designed to equip students with the necessary skills and knowledge to excel in a variety of IT roles within technology development. The course covers a broad range of topics, including building students' proficiency in various programming languages and platforms, the application and analysis of modern software engineering tools, and security and privacy aspects of technology design. In addition to core information technology development competencies, students undertake one major. These are specialised streams that delve into the intricacies of developing advanced software systems, harnessing the power of interconnected devices that can sense and act in the physical world, and higher level information systems considerations that drive decision-making in technology implementation. These majors are designed to cater to the diverse interests of students and the evolving demands of industry.

faculty: Faculty of Humanities, Arts, Social Sciences and Education
description: The Bachelor of International Studies is a three-year degree covering global social developments and world affairs from a variety of disciplinary perspectives. The focus is comparative and contemporary, and the program also enables you, should you wish, to combine international studies with a foreign language. Core units cover cross-cultural communication, the human impact on the environment, international economy, international relations in the Asia Pacific, peace, conflict, and social change. You can choose two from five majors: Global Politics and Peace; Human Futures and Global Challenges; International Law; International Business; Languages and Cultures. The Global Politics and Peace major engages with the most challenging political issues of the 21st century. It covers key events such as the 9/11 attacks, the Global Financial Crisis (GFC) and its aftermath, populist politics, China’s rising power, and ongoing conflicts and wars. What are the sources of stability and instability in the current world (dis)order? What are the major threats to peace and how might these be addressed? Political science and peace studies are at the core of this major, with relevant contributions from history and sociology. The Human Futures and Global Challenges major includes contributions from disciplines such as human geography, philosophy, and sociology. It examines the key social, environmental, and ethical challenges facing humanity, including climate change, population, the environment and natural resources; conflict and human rights; religion and politics; migration and refugees. The focus is international and contemporary, but you can also study Australia’s past and present place in the global order. The major in International Business introduces you to key issues in contemporary economics and business studies. The core program covers macroeconomics and international political economy, including the key economics of India and China. Electives include such topics as cross-cultural communication and management, international finance, professional skills, indigenous development, and small business and digital marketing. In the innovative International Law major, after completing Foundations of Law in your first year, you can choose from a wide array of units. Hot topics include navigating trade wars, human rights advocacy at the United Nations; wildlife trafficking; global governance of water, mining, fisheries and forests; maritime security notably the South China sea dispute; and combating the nefarious underworld of transnational crime. In the Languages and Cultures major you can pursue a language and its culture to an advanced level (Chinese, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese or Spanish). This typically includes an exploration of that country’s history, society, art, material culture, literature and film. As part of your language major, you have the option of taking an in-country language that is tailored to your interests (ICLU300). This flexible degree can be studied at our beautiful regional Armidale campus or online with cutting-edge technology. Successful graduates may, on the recommendation of the Head of School, continue to an honours year. The honours program comprises advanced coursework and a thesis on a topic of interest.

description: UNE boasts one of Australia's largest law schools outside a capital city, as well as being an early adopter of innovative technology in the delivery of its law programs. courseName: Bachelor of Medical Science and Doctor of Medicine
description: The Joint Medical Program (JMP) is a two stage five year program comprising of a Bachelor of Medical Science (stage one) and Doctor of Medicine (stage two), offered jointly in partnership by the University of Newcastle and the University of New England. The program consists of three phases across the five years where stage one comprises of Phase 1 and 2. Phase 1 focuses on the biomedical, behavioural and social sciences and is taught through problem based learning. In problem based learning tutorials, students learn about the body systems such as the cardiac and respiratory systems using clinical presentations as a trigger to guide the learning. The tutorials are supported by sessions in the laboratory, lectures from biomedical scientists or clinicians, and practical clinical skills teaching. During Phase 1, students will be introduced to the clinical environment with clinical placements in the hospital, nursing homes and general practice to practice history taking and clinical examinations. Phase 2 is one year in duration and consists of clinical placements in medicine and surgery in hospital and general practice/community-based care. Case-based learning replaces the problem based learning tutorial from Phase 1 and builds on the foundational knowledge of Phase 1 with clinical cases being the trigger to guide the learning. During Phase 2, students will consolidate their research method skills and develop a research project proposal for a project that will be completed in stage 2 (Phase 3). Phase 3 is clinically orientated where students rotate through clinical placements, undertake a Student Selected Pathway and complete a Structured Reflective Option. In Year 4, students complete placements in Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Paediatrics, Medicine and Psychiatry. Year 5 is termed a pre-internship year which is designed to prepare students for internship. The clinical placements are in Surgery, Medicine, Critical Care and Trauma, and General Practice. During Year 4, students will consolidate their research method skills and complete the project proposed in Stage One (Year 3). The Student Selected Pathway is an opportunity for students to explore special interest areas within the broad categories of: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples health; Global Health; Health Professional Education; Laboratory Medicine; Rural Health; and Entrepreneurship. Time is allocated in Year 4 for course and preparatory work in Year 4 for the experience in Year 5. The Structured Reflective Option is an opportunity to explore other areas of interest and/or to consolidate knowledge and skills. This is available in Year 4. On completion of stage one, students will have completed the requirements for the Bachelor of Medical Science. On completion of Stage Two, students will have completed the requirements for the Doctor of Medicine. To graduate from the Joint Medical Program, students must complete both stage one and two. The Bachelor of Medical Science and the Doctor of Medicine will be awarded on a single testamur on completion of stage two. This is an approved Student Income Support course. Eligible students may apply for Youth Allowance or Austudy.

description: The Bachelor of Nursing prepares graduates as knowledgeable, thoughtful, evidence-based practitioners equipped to provide person-centred care and contribute to the maintenance and development of the nursing profession. Nursing education integrates and applies knowledge from biomedical, psychological, and social sciences unique to the discipline. UNE students are supported in developing inquiring minds, becoming lifelong learners, and being responsive to the varying needs of people within a changing society. The knowledge and skills attained enable our graduates to be change agents in the profession and the healthcare industry. Our course encourages nurses to consider working in rural areas through content that familiarises students with nursing in a rural context. UNE supports students undertaking the Bachelor of Nursing to meet course learning outcomes aligned with the Registered Nurse Standards for Practice (NMBA, 2016). Teaching and learning strategies engage students with a well-established, blended learning environment. description: The Bachelor of Nutrition and Health Science provides a comprehensive education in nutrition science, health promotion, and food sustainability. This innovative program equips students with scientific knowledge of nutrient metabolism and human physiology alongside practical skills in nutritional assessment and evidence-based dietary advice. Through carefully scaffolded learning experiences, students develop expertise in analysing the relationships between nutrition and health maintenance, while gaining valuable professional capabilities through work-integrated learning opportunities. The multidisciplinary curriculum integrates perspectives from biomedical science, health, and agricultural sustainability, preparing graduates for diverse career pathways in clinical nutrition, public health, food industry innovation, and research. With its focus on both scientific rigor and practical application, this program develops graduates who can effectively address contemporary nutrition challenges and contribute to improved health outcomes in communities.

The course is geared toward individuals who are preparing themselves to be leaders of tomorrow whether in government, church, military, statutory, non-profit or commercial organisations. This course recognises students' professional background by granting full credit for any previous studies, training and work experience, and thereby helping students take the step into tertiary education. The UNE Bachelor of Organisational Leadership brings together a highly structured, well-rounded program that concentrates on managerial issues ranging from leadership to organisational change, ethics and strategic planning. It will enable you to gain real-world contemporary skills and important competences needed to thrive as a leader in the workforce of the future. Choose from units that allow you to learn how to develop digital literacy, structure and present successful business proposals or study communication between people of differing cultural backgrounds in different social and professional contexts. Alternatively, add a unit in accounting and finance for business or employment relations.

description: Students enrolled in the Bachelor of Pharmacy with Honours develop a strong foundation in essential core skills in relevant pharmaceutical sciences, which is then integrated with contemporary knowledge and application to pharmacokinetics, pharmacotherapeutics and pharmacy practice. To develop practical and clinical skills, course work is complemented by seven weeks (approx. 270 hours) of clinical placement. The first two weeks are completed in community pharmacy during second year, then in fourth year students undertake the remaining hours in three full time blocks in both community and hospital pharmacy. The fourth year placement blocks will include at least one week full time in a rural community pharmacy. The Bachelor of Pharmacy with Honours is offered as a 4-year full time undergraduate course available via online education*. The University of New England is the first university in Australia to offer a Bachelor of Pharmacy with Honours via online education delivery. The degree must be completed within ten years from the date of commencement. This program has been granted accreditation by the Australian Pharmacy Council and is approved by the Pharmacy Board of Australia as a qualification leading to registration as a pharmacist in Australia. On successful completion of the pharmacy program you will be eligible for provisional registration as a pharmacist with the Pharmacy Board of Australia. However, to practice in Australia pharmacists must be registered with the Pharmacy Board of Australia and meet their registration standards. Further information is available at https://www.pharmacyboard.gov.au/Registration-Standards. *This course includes units with mandatory on campus intensive schools. Refer to Additional Information section and individual units in UNE Handbook for details.

description: Why study the Bachelor of Psychological Science at UNE? The Bachelor of Psychological Science provides a thorough grounding in psychology. You study more Psychology units as you progress through each year of the course. This provides an opportunity to explore other areas of interest in the early years of your degree but achieve a thorough grounding in Psychology by the time you graduate. The result is a balanced education, as well as a specialisation in Psychology. The degree includes Psychology units as diverse as Social Psychology (the study of human social behaviour), Biopsychology (the study of the biological bases of behaviour), Individual Differences and Assessment (study of individual differences in personality, intelligence and behaviour), and Psychopathology (the study of psychological disorders). In addition, an optional Major in Counselling or Community Services or Minor in Criminology is available within the course. Combining online study with mandatory online intensive schools, the Major in Counselling is ideally suited to individuals wishing to gain theoretical knowledge and practice-based skills in counselling. Graduates of the Bachelor of Psychological Science (Counselling Major) who enrol in UNE’s Graduate Diploma of Counselling or Master of Counselling will be granted 12 credit points of Advanced Standing based on their admission to candidature. The Community Services Major provides theoretical and practical skills in case management with the opportunity to undertake 2 separate work placements to provide real world experience in the Community Services sector. Community Services is a major growth area for employment so undertaking this Major will place you in a good position for future employment in the sector. description: The University of New England offers a flexible approach to the study of law. UNE boasts one of Australia's largest law schools outside a capital city, as well as being an early adopter of innovative technology in the delivery of its law programs. Studying law in conjunction with another discipline gives you the potential to take an interdisciplinary approach in both your studies and in your future employment. Graduates with law and science background will understand both the legal framework, processes and the technical factors relating to areas such as genetics, zoology and physiology, particularly where research ethics and the commercial exploitation of research are being considered. Science component : On completion of 144 credit points including all requirements for the BSc component of the double degree program, students with a meritorious academic record may be permitted to enrol for the Bachelor of Science with Honours. The Honours year in Science requires the completion of a research project and the submission of a thesis embodying a literature review and the results of the research project. Law component: There are a range of employment options from which to choose. Graduates who wish to be admitted to practice as a solicitor, barrister or legal practitioner anywhere in Australia will also have to undertake a course of professional legal training (PLT). This can consist of approximately half a year's full-time training, undertaken internally or externally, or of equivalent part-time training. In some jurisdictions, it may be possible to do articles of clerkship instead. Because the system adopted varies from jurisdiction to jurisdiction, enquiries should be made to the admission authority in the state or territory in which you intend to practice; this is usually a committee of the Supreme Court of that State or Territory or a special body set up to administer admissions to the legal profession. Additional information can be found on the School of Law page. Students who complete the Honours Pathway may be awarded the degree of Bachelor of Laws with Honours. To be admitted to the Honours stream, candidates must have completed 72 credit points of law units at UNE with a grade point average (GPA) of 5.5 or better.

faculty: Faculty of Medicine and Health
description: The Bachelor of Social Work provides graduates with the theoretical and practical skills required to work as a professional social worker, an occupation that the Australian government predicts will continue to experience very strong growth. Graduates are eligible for membership of the Australian Association of Social Workers. UNE social work graduates typically work with disadvantaged and marginalised individuals, groups, and communities using a social justice and trauma-informed framework in counselling, advocacy, and community development to enhance people's health and well-being. Social workers address barriers, inequality and injustices faced by many groups, particularly those who are socially excluded. UNE's social work program embraces a framework that examines the dynamic interaction of human behaviour and complex social interactions and institutions. Curriculum development within the course involves ongoing engagement and dialogue with practitioners and consumers to ensure not only a high- quality learning experience for students but also the development and maintenance of partnerships within communities both domestically and internationally. Covering all the core requirements of an accredited professional social work degree, the Bachelor of Social Work at UNE equips graduates for the many challenges involved in Social Work practice locally, nationally and internationally, including within rural and remote communities; and focuses on rights-based practice, mental health, diversity, Indigenous peoples and Indigenous ways of knowing, being and doing, child protection and the law. The course incorporates 1000 hours of professional fieldwork placement supervised by experienced practitioners in diverse social work settings locally and overseas. Students can choose to study either on campus or online, with mandatory, on-campus intensive schools for students enrolled in online study mode. This course is accredited with the Australian Association of Social Workers. All students, including those enrolled online, are required to participate in on-campus learning for a minimum of 20 days/150hrs over the duration of the course. This requirement is met via attendance at the mandatory intensive schools associated with some of the core units for online students and/or via face-to-face mandatory classes throughout the trimester for on campus students. This requirement is stipulated by the Australian Social Work Education and Accreditation Standards (ASWEAS).

description: The Bachelor of Sustainability at UNE provides a unique opportunity to develop skills and an understanding of sustainability in a holistic manner, integrating the social sciences and humanities with the environmental sciences and natural resource management. Going beyond traditional disciplinary boundaries, and transcending the old 'arts-sciences' divide, we adopt a multi- and inter-disciplinary approach to sustainability, and graduates gain an understanding of social and community sustainability as well as ecologically sustainable development - a great advantage in the growing 'green collar' job market. UNE was the first university in Australia to offer this degree and ours remains a step-ahead, offering targeted, career-orientated majors depending on whether you would like to work with communities, design and implement policy, or work in environmental protection or cultural heritage management. Whether you would like to work in the public sector, private sector or in the non-government field, the potential avenues are endless. Workplace experience is facilitated during the degree and you can also draw upon the expertise of our industry-based Course Advisory Board as well as the guidance and mentorship of our cutting-edge researchers and academics. Our staff are at the forefront of their fields, they are passionate about sustainability and as well as teaching, they also conduct research in: ecosystems, environmental law and policy, carbon and water trading and climate change - and these are just a few examples! UNE has a long history of supporting social and economic well-being and environmental health right across Australia. This was recognised at the 2010 NSW Green Globe awards, where UNE received a 10 year sustainability certificate for its extensive accomplishments in resource management and education for sustainability. So, if you would like to work with people in building a better world then this degree is for you! You will be equipped with the ability to understand the complexities of the environmental and social problems which beset our society, as well as the problem-solving abilities needed to build a sustainable future. You will study a diverse variety of subjects from a broad range of disciplines, together providing a unique focus on sustainability integrating environmental management, geography, law, psychology, social science, economics and policy studies. You can major in Environmental Resilience, Environmental Governance, Governance and Regulation, Community Engagement, Development or Cultural Heritage Management and Water Sustainability. Each major has mandatory units and you can supplement these with your choice of electives, and you may also undertake work placements if you wish. Read on for more details!

description: This degree leads to a professional career in planning, with employment opportunities in both city and country. Planners need to be familiar with a wide range of issues and the degree provides a broad general education in all major areas of planning and urban design, including land use planning, social planning, economic planning, transport planning, environmental planning, professionalism and ethics, and environmental and planning law. Work experience is an important part of the program and means that students receive a hands-on education, opportunities to put their learning into practice and a head-start in terms of gaining on-the-job experience. description: Zoology is the science of studying and understanding animals living on land, in freshwater or in the sea. It is the branch of biology that covers behaviour, classification, evolution, conservation, distribution, ecology and natural history, but also includes biochemistry and physiology, palaeontology, molecular biology and genetics, and the structure and function of animals. Zoology students will undertake studies in a range of zoological disciplines including animal behaviour; animal ecology; environmental and comparative physiology; entomology; parasitology and vertebrate and invertebrate zoology. Students will also complete a Course Major in either Animal Ecology, Applied Zoology, Natural History or Palaeobiology. Our mission is to: - provide students with a thorough knowledge of the diversity of the animal kingdom and an understanding of how that diversity arose through a research-led-and-informed curriculum; - enable students to graduate with practical laboratory and fieldwork skills, critical problem-solving skills, and excellent communication skills; - harness the unique attributes of UNE's location nationally and internationally and access to a unique fauna, unmatched online education experience, and above-world class research credentials to provide undergraduate students with a holistic education within zoology; - prepare students for further study or employment across the wide range of disciplines within which zoology is critical; provide broad understanding of zoology for students who do not aspire to continue with employment in the area; and - instil students with an appreciation of the many facets that make up zoological sciences. Students considering further study and interested in research should consider completing ERS381 as a capstone unit in their chosen major. To discuss individual options, interested students should consult with the Course Coordinator or a member of staff from a research area in which they are interested. A fourth Honours year is available to students with an above average academic record. Study is undertaken in one of the disciplines chosen for specialisation leading to the award of Bachelor of Science with Honours. BSc(Hons) graduates who achieve the appropriate level of Honours are eligible to apply to enrol for a research Master degree or the degree of Doctor of Philosophy (PhD). Q Fever: It is a condition that all students enrolled in this course must be vaccinated against Q Fever (unless initial skin test indicates pre-existing immunity). This must be completed as soon as possible and by no later than the end of the first trimester of study. Q Fever screening and vaccination can be arranged through the University Medical Centre, or through your own GP. The cost of the vaccination program is separate to tuition fees. description: The Diploma of Town Planning has been designed to provide an opportunity for university study for people who may never have considered nor undertaken university study before. It also provides a pathway to further university study. The Diploma is an introductory course suited to: people who are looking at widening their employment prospects; people seeking a career change and who are interested in entering a career in planning;local government employees who wish to develop their skills and career prospects; TAFE students who have completed a CERT IV (in any area);people currently working in the planning system in a clerical/administrative capacity; and unqualified planning assistants. The program consists of eight units. It includes four compulsory first-year units, followed by four elective units. The Diploma will normally take people two years to complete, at a rate of two units per trimester. However the programme is flexible and people may complete at different rates. The course is delivered online and can be undertaken from any location. There is no compulsory on-campus attendance, although some of the units in the program have non-mandatory intensive schools which provide an opportunity for face-to-face instruction and interaction with other students. The online learning environment and support provided for the course also provides many opportunities for interaction with lecturers and students. Completion of the Diploma does not in itself lead to membership of the Planning Institute of Australia - although for anyone who would like to go on to further study, units passed toward the Diploma can be credited towards the Bachelor of Urban and Regional Planning at UNE. The UNE Bachelor of Urban and Regional Planning is fully accredited with the Planning Institute of Australia .

faculty: Learning and Teaching Transformation
description: The Foundation Program is a program of study providing students with an alternative pathway for admission to an undergraduate course at UNE. The aim of the course is to provide students with the knowledge, skills, and abilities required to become active, confident, and self-directed learners, in order to successfully undertake an undergraduate course with an ATAR requirement of 77.10 or lower. Completion of the Foundation Program provides the basis for admission to most undergraduate courses at UNE. Domestic students are exempt from the student contribution amount for HECS. To be eligible for the Foundation Program you must fall under one of the following circumstances; You left school before completing the HSC or equivalent, and have been working for at least 12 months; or You have completed the HSC or equivalent, but your high school results were too low to gain entry to a university degree program; or You have completed your high school education and have been in the workforce for a number of years, and have no other entry path into university; or You have not formally studied before, and you wish to build your academic skills to ensure your success at university study; or You have partially complete prior studies and need to enhance your academic skills. Students receive mentoring and additional tutorial support in the Enabling units (ENAB101 and ENAB102). If you complete the Listed Unit in the Foundation Program, which is part of the course in which you later choose to enrol, you will receive advanced standing for this unit. The two Enabling units (ENAB101 and ENAB102) include a range of activities and tasks that support students in developing their abilities and identities as university-level learners. Results in these Enabling units are grades satisfactory or unsatisfactory. ENAB101 and ENAB102 do not count towards any course but provide students with the skills and confidence required for successful undergraduate study.
duration: Up to 4 years Part-time

description: With flexible online delivery, the UNE Graduate Certificate in School Psychology provides you with specialised practice skills required to work in educational settings. This course is designed to be studied alongside UNE's Master of Professional Psychology or Master of Psychology (Clinical) to ensure graduates are job-ready and competitive for internship opportunities in school psychology positions. A psychologist in schools is often the first point of referral for children and young people who present with a wide variety of difficulties of varying complexity and severity. This course will future fit your career by preparing you with practical skills to navigate the ethical, professional and practice dilemmas encountered in educational settings. Core modules within these units will provide a grounding in evidence-based and culturally responsive assessment and intervention techniques that will equip you to work with children, adolescents and young adults. Working in schools requires a high level of critical thinking, communication skills and effective interprofessional working capability. This course will facilitate the application of these skills, alongside best practice in professional psychology, with individual clients, parents/carers, groups, multi-disciplinary colleagues and the wider school community.

You will develop core interpersonal skills and strategies, key to engaging young people and providing effective support. Building your critical thinking skills, you will learn about the ethical, legal and policy context of your work in schools. Strengthening collaborative practice, this course builds an integrated understanding of teaching obligations, responsibilities and practical approaches to challenging behaviour. This course will provide you with the confidence, knowledge and advanced certification to clearly define your role in wellbeing support. Whether you are an existing professional or moving into a new role of wellbeing support, this course will ensure that you are equipped with the specialist knowledge and skills required to holistically meet wellbeing needs in a school setting.

description: The Graduate Certificate in Science is a course designed for students who wish to expand on their undergraduate program. description: The Graduate Diploma in Counselling is informed and underpinned by Humanistic and Existential counselling philosophies which deal with questions of meaning and freedom, grapple with what it means to be human and emphasise the value of individual and collective agency. Humanistic counselling approaches offer a way of 'being' in the world and a focus on the person rather than the symptoms. Humanistic approaches require a commitment on the part of the counsellor to self-acknowledge and, at the same time, to the understanding that this self-knowledge is never fully attained. This requires a degree of emotional and psychological agility. Your success in this award will be strongly linked to your willingness to connect with others and to explore what emerges during these connections. You may find the learning experience in this course to be different to past study experiences. Counsellor training requires independent, self-directed and reflexive learning. The course aims to provide you with what we would like you to provide to your clients: a growth-promoting climate. In this growth-promoting climate, your engagement with each other will assist with your development of genuineness, acceptance, caring, compassion, and empathy. The Graduate Diploma in Counselling will prepare you to work as a university-qualified registered counsellor in a diverse range of counselling contexts. Combine online study with mandatory intensive schools, the course is ideally suited to individuals wishing to gain an industry-recognised , tertiary-level qualification whilst continuing to meet their work and family commitments. As part of the award, students can complete either the Generalist Counselling Pathway, the Mental Health Practice Pathway or the Counselling Placement Pathway. These three pathways, in addition to providing graduates with core theoretical and practical skills in counselling, permit students to focus on a specific area of professional practice. The Generalist Counselling Pathway develops graduates’ skills and knowledge in relation to counselling for loss and grief, counselling for trauma, relationship counselling, and working with children and adolescents. The Mental Health Practice Pathway, based on the Mental Health Competencies in the National Standards for the Mental Health Workforce as part of the National Mental Health Strategy, equips graduates to work effectively in the mental health field. The Counselling Placement Pathway includes 40 hours of face-to-face counselling; 10 hours of clinical supervision and 150 hours of agency-based activities, and offers students the opportunity to engage in work integrated learning in a counselling context. The Graduate Diploma in Counselling provides a direct pathway to the Master of Counselling at UNE and is accredited by the Australian Counselling Association (ACA), a national peak association, and Australia's largest single registration body for counsellors and psychotherapists. Student membership with the ACA is available while undertaking the course, with professional membership eligibility after graduation. Graduates who engage in ongoing professional development are also eligible to be listed on the Australian Register of Counsellors and Psychotherapists (ARCAP), an independent national register of qualified counsellors and psychotherapists.

description: Data is a vital asset valued by virtually every organisation in the world. It provides the basis for sensible, evidence-based decision making, and the ability to manage and make sense of data is a key skill in the modern workplace. In the last decade, streams of data of various types have grown in volume and velocity such that they require specialist skills in order to get the most value from them. Data scientists are responsible for building intelligent systems, mastering intuitive processes and bringing structure to the vast quantities of data to unlock the potential for improvement and competitive advantage. The Graduate Diploma in Data Science will provide students with the required knowledge and practical skills to analyse and manage data. This course will prepare students to solve complex and challenging problems and provides an opportunity to complete a comprehensive capstone project experience, through enrolment in a Science Research Project unit. The Graduate Diploma in Data Science is a course that complements existing skill sets and provides opportunity to up-skill for positions that have a rigorous quantitative aspect.

faculty: Learning and Teaching Transformation
description: The HSC University Pathways course is for high-achieving students who want to get a head start on their university study while still at school. The course lets students choose up to two units from a wide selection of university units and study them while in Year 12. These units will supplement their HSC education and provide advanced standing into a university course of their choice. Get started by downloading and completing the HSC University Pathways Entry Form . At UNE, this program is unique as it is offered as a Commonwealth Supported Place (CSP), meaning that if you are an eligible domestic student, you may defer your tuition through HECS-HELP. For a list of units available to students please see the program of study. These units are featured in a number of the most popular UNE degree courses. These include, but are not limited to: Bachelor of Arts (including Law and Teaching variants) Bachelor of Criminology Bachelor of Historical Inquiry and Practice Bachelor of Languages Bachelor of Laws Bachelor of Media and Communication Bachelor of Music Bachelor of Psychological Science Bachelor of Science (including Law and Teaching variants) Bachelor of Urban and Regional Planning The Bachelor of Arts and Bachelor of Science have many other associated degrees that also include these units. It is strongly advised that students, parents and school advisors contact UNE to seek advice on which units are appropriate for entry into degrees. Step by step to applying: Step One: Download the HSC University Pathways Entry Form . Step Two: Write your NSW Education Standards Authority (NESA) number and name at the top of each page. Fill in Part A of the form. Step Three: Gather together any additional documentation required for your application. Step Four: Deliver your form to your Principal (or whoever is responsible for them at your school, such as your Careers Advisor). Step Five: Relax while your school completes Part B of the form and submits it to UNE on your behalf. Step Six: You will get an email advising you that your HSC Pathways application has been received by UNE. Step Seven: UNE will review the application, and you will be emailed the outcome. Step Eight: If successful, you accept your offer of admission directly through UNE.
duration: 1 Trimester Part-time

description: UNE's Master of Applied Linguistics (MAAL) degree provides a professional qualification for those working in language teaching, language program management, TESOL, social services, health, education and the law, as well as those who work with linguistic and cultural minorities. No previous linguistics study is required, and the degree can be completed in as little as two years. Subject to meeting eligibility requirements, you can choose to exit the course with a Graduate Certificate in Applied Linguistics after completing four units, or with a Graduate Diploma in Applied Linguistics after completing eight units. UNE's MAAL degree was Australia's first fully online Masters degree in Applied Linguistics, and our staff have over 15 years of experience in offering this high-quality interactive postgraduate course using the latest multimedia technology. You will be part of a global classroom, interacting with your lecturers and with students from more than 30 countries via online discussion forums. You'll explore languages of the world, language acquisition, language in education, language in legal and other professional contexts, and intercultural communication - all at a time and place that suit your work or family commitments. Choose from one of three majors: the General Major, leading to the Master of Applied Linguistics (General), or the Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages Major, leading to the Master of Applied Linguistics (TESOL), or the Intercultural Communication for Business and Services Major, leading to the Master of Applied Linguistics (ICBS). The TESOL Major incorporates specialist TESOL units including a professional practicum which can be completed in a wide range of contexts. Students who wish to pursue further research can take a 24 credit point independent research project, LING599, which meets the requirements for entry to a PhD (entry to LING599 is selective). The Master of Applied Linguistics (TESOL) is an approved Student Income Support course. Eligible students may apply for Youth Allowance or Austudy.

description: Artificial intelligence (AI) encompasses a spectrum of technologies, algorithms, and methodologies that are aimed at simulating human intelligence in machines, allowing them to mimic cognitive functions such as learning and problem solving. Unlike traditional computer applications that are programmed for specific tasks, AI systems possess the ability to adapt and improve their performance through experience. AI plays an increasingly important role in our lives and now drives many of the experiences and interactions in our day-to-day activities. In essence, AI's importance stems from its ability to augment human capabilities, address challenges, and unlock new possibilities across many domains. The Master of Artificial Intelligence provides students with the required knowledge and practical skills to build systems based around AI technologies. Students will develop expertise in areas including machine learning, computer vision and data processing and apply these to solve complex problems. The program includes an industry–based project or research thesis where the students can further develop the skills introduced across the course. The Master of Artificial Intelligence is a postgraduate course that complements any existing skillset and provides opportunity to upskill for positions that have a rigorous quantitative aspect. Graduates from this program will be well-equipped to tackle complex AI challenges and play a leading role in the future development of AI solutions globally. Master of Artificial Intelligence graduates are eligible to apply for admission to PhD candidature, upon successful completion of the thesis.

description: Our MBA allows you to expand your professional skills and knowledge to achieve your career goals. The degree provides you with a comprehensive set of skills in the key fields of decision making, ethics, management, marketing and strategy needed to operate in a globalised economy. We have a diverse range of admission pathways. If you have a bachelor's degree or higher, plus at least two years relevant work experience you will be eligible for admission to the MBA. If you do not have a bachelor's degree, you can undertake a Graduate Certificate in either Accounting, Agribusiness, Business, Health Management, Human Resource Management or Management and this will enable you to articulate through to the MBA. The Graduate Certificate pathways require only a Diploma, Advanced Diploma, or relevant work experience (up to six years depending on the Graduate Certificate) for admission. The focus of our 12 unit MBA is to give you a broad and contemporary perspective on management challenges in leading people and making decisions. You can complete your MBA via coursework alone, or coursework and a major research project, or through a combination of core units and a major in human resource management or in health management. You can also apply to progress to PhD studies if you have chosen to complete a major research project as part of your course. The major in Human Resource Management is accredited by the Australian Human Resources Institute (AHRI). Our MBA will challenge you to think in new ways and encourage you to apply that learning immediately. From day one, you will be testing your knowledge against the real world, integrating it into your thinking and becoming a more effective and adaptable manager in the process. At UNE, online study is about flexibility and support that can only be provided by a university that has long understood the challenges faced by adults balancing work, family/life and study. We have three teaching periods (trimesters), commencing in February, June and October, giving you greater choice about when and how much you study each year. All units are delivered through our online learning platform and are developed by skilled educational designers in order to maximise your learning experience. There is the opportunity to attend Optional face-to-face weekend schools across a range of units which will provide you with the opportunity to come together to collaborate with your fellow students, and meet our highly qualified teaching staff in person. Our units are taught by internationally recognised academics who have a strong track record in research and a wealth of experience in business and industry. Staff are continually commended by graduates for their enthusiastic and proactive engagement with students. We offer a highly personalised education experience, helping you navigate your studies and to achieve your career aspirations.

description: Information and computing technology affects all aspects of modern life and there is a worldwide shortage of ICT professionals. Its applications now include, not only commerce and science, but also health, education, engineering, transport, government, entertainment, sport, and social networking. It has become so complex that only well-educated professionals are capable of developing and applying ICT systems in modern organisations. Even professionals in other disciplines need a sound understanding of ICT to perform their own jobs efficiently and effectively. Emphasis is placed upon the structured design of algorithms for computer-based implementations of real-life tasks. The interactive execution, analysis and use of programs are discussed together with advanced algorithmic designs and programming techniques; informal notions of program specification and verification; a high-level description of the abstract architecture of the von Neumann machine; numerical and non-numerical applications; and social issues. This course provides a comprehensive, modern postgraduate education in the principles and practice of ICT together with the opportunity to gain enhanced knowledge and skills in research. Master of Computer Science graduates are eligible to apply for admission to PhD candidature, upon successful completion of the thesis.

faculty: Faculty of Medicine and Health
description: The Master of Counselling is informed and underpinned by Humanistic and Existential counselling philosophies which deal with questions of meaning and freedom, grapple with what it means to be human and emphasise the value of individual and collective agency. Humanistic counselling approaches offer a way of 'being' in the world and a focus on the person rather than the symptoms. Humanistic approaches require a commitment on the part of the counsellor to self-knowledge and, at the same time, to the understanding that this self-knowledge is never fully attained. This requires a degree of emotional and psychological agility. Your success in this award will be strongly linked to your willingness to connect with others and to explore what emerges during these connections. You may find the learning experience in this course to be different to past study experiences. Counsellor training requires independent, self-directed and reflexive learning. The course aims to provide you with what we would like you to provide to your clients: a growth-promoting climate. In this growth-promoting climate, your engagement with each other will assist with your development of genuineness, acceptance, caring, compassion, and accurate empathic understanding. Combining online study with mandatory intensive schools, the course is ideally suited to individuals wishing to gain an industry-recognised qualification whilst continuing to meet their work and family commitments. As part of the award, students can complete either the Generalist Counselling Pathway, the Mental Health Practice Pathway or the Counselling Placement Pathway. These three pathways, in addition to providing graduates with core theoretical and practical skills in counselling, permit students to focus on a specific area of professional practice. The Generalist Counselling Pathway develops graduates’ skills and knowledge in relation to counselling for loss and grief, counselling for trauma, systemic and relationship counselling, and working with children and adolescents. The Mental Health Practice Pathway, based on the Mental Health Competencies in the National Standards for the Mental Health Workforce as part of the National Mental Health Strategy, equips graduates to work effectively in the mental health field. The Counselling Placement Pathway includes 40 hours of face-to-face counselling; 10 hours of clinical supervision and 150 hours of agency-based activities, and offers students the opportunity to engage in work integrated learning in a counselling context. The course provides a pathway to the UNE Doctor of Philosophy for those students who meet the other entry requirements to that program. The Master of Counselling is accredited by the Australian Counselling Association (ACA), a national peak association, and Australia's largest single registration body for counsellors and psychotherapists. Student membership with the ACA is available while undertaking the course, with professional membership eligibility after graduation. Graduates who engage in ongoing professional development are also eligible to be listed on the Australian Register of Counsellors and Psychotherapists (ARCAP), an independent national register of qualified counsellors and psychotherapists.

description: Data is a vital asset valued by virtually every organisation in the world. It provides the basis for sensible, evidence-based decision making, and the ability to manage and make sense of data is a key skill in the modern workplace. In the last decade, streams of data of various types have grown in volume and velocity such that they require specialist skills in order to get the most value from them. Data scientists are responsible for buildng intelligent systems, mastering intuitive proesses and bringing structure to the vast quantities of data to unlock the potential for improvement and competitive advantage. They will learn how to deal with large and diverse data sets and apply a variety of technologies to extract meaning from them. description: The Master of Nursing Practice (Preregistration) (MNPP) is designed for international and domestic students and prepares graduates as beginning-level Registered Nurses who are knowledgeable, thoughtful, and evidence-based practitioners equipped to provide person-centred care and contribute to the maintenance and development of the nursing profession. Nursing education integrates and applies knowledge from biomedical, psychological, and social sciences unique to the discipline. UNE students are supported in developing inquiring minds, becoming lifelong learners, and being responsive to the varying needs of people within a changing society. The knowledge and skills gained during this course enable our graduates to be agents of change in the nursing profession and the broader healthcare industry. Our course encourages nurses to consider working in rural areas through content that familiarises students with nursing in a rural context. UNE supports students undertaking the MNPP to meet course learning outcomes aligned with the Registered Nurse Standards for Practice (NMBA, 2016). The MNPP is a professional entry degree, leading to eligibility for Registered Nurse status. Teaching and learning strategies engage students with a well-established, engaging blended learning environment. The course (under Admission Rule A) can be studied over 2 years (24 calendar months) of full-time study, or part-time equivalent. Applicants who have an unrestricted registration as a Midwife with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) (under Admission Rule B) can complete in 2 years (21 calendar months) of full-time study or part-time equivalent. Please Note International students on a Student Visa admitted under Rule A will have an on campus intake in Trimester 3 at Armidale or UNE Sydney (Parramatta). As quotas apply at each campus you may not be offered your campus of choice. International students on a Student Visa admitted to Rule B will have an on campus intake in Trimester 1 at Armidale only. In addition to the above on campus offerings, International students admitted on any visa, other than a Student Visa, that allows study within Australia, will also have an online full-time intake in Armidale in Trimester 3 (Rule A) or Trimester 1 (Rule B). This program of study is undertaken in Australia. Students cannot undertake any professional education practice units while outside Australia. UNE Sydney (Parramatta) is only available to International Students admitted under Rule A. International students commencing as a full-time student, on any visa, must remain a full-time student for the entirety of their enrolment. Due to a course quota, this course is subject to closing without notice if the quota is met. Rule B is not on offer in 2026. You cannot defer your place in the course if you receive an offer to study the MNPP under Rules A or B. If you are unable to commence, you must reapply for admission. The Master of Nursing Practice (Preregistration) is an approved Student Income Support course. Eligible students may apply for Youth Allowance or Austudy.

description: A Master of Public Health (MPH) is an internationally-recognised qualification, favoured by those desiring careers in Public Health. In contrast to a traditional Master of Public Health award, UNE’s Master of Public Health (One Health) equips students with an integrative approach to humans, animals, plants, and environmental health. UNE’s focus on One Health within its Master of Public Health degree, together with the choice of three minors: environmental health, organizational health and global health gives graduates a distinct advantage in the public health field. The Master of Public Health (One Health) has the added advantage of providing students with the opportunity to integrate theory and practice from multiple disciplines and sectors at the local, national and international levels. The course is delivered fully online, in full-time and part-time modes, to ensure maximum flexibility and the maintenance of a work, life and study balance. Students will complete their study program with a capstone unit in which they consolidate their theoretical learning of Public Health with a 'real world' action research project. Master of Public Health (One Health) students are typically individuals who plan to build a career within the realm of population health, health promotion, epidemiology, and leadership roles in public and private practices including departments of health, local health districts, and non-government organisations, nationally and internationally. Students admitted under Rule A may be able to study part-time only depending on the minor chosen; Students admitted under Rule B will only be able to study part-time only
