description: The Master of Social Work (Qualifying) provides graduates with the theoretical and practical skills required to work as a professional social worker, an occupation that the Australian government predicts will continue to experience very strong growth. This course is accredited with the Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW) and graduates are eligible to become a member of the AASW. Social workers typically work with disadvantaged and marginalised individuals, groups, and communities within a social justice and human rights framework in counselling, advocacy, and the enhancement of health and well-being. Social workers address the barriers, inequality and injustices faced by many groups in our community, and engage with the many challenges involved in social work practice locally, nationally and internationally, including within rural and remote communities. UNE's social work program embraces a framework that examines the dynamics of human behaviour, institutions and complex social interactions. Covering the core requirements of an accredited professional social work degree, the MSW (Qualifying) at UNE emphasises practice in rural and complex community environments, and focuses on rights-based practice, mental health, Indigenous peoples, child protection and the law. The course incorporates the mandatory 1000 hours of professional fieldwork placement supervised by experienced practitioners in diverse social work settings locally and overseas. Study requirements allow students choice to study either on-campus or online. All students, including those enrolled online, are required to participate in on-campus learning for a minimum of 20 days/150hrs over the duration of the course. This requirement is met via attendance at the mandatory intensive schools associated with some of the core units for online students and/or via face-to-face mandatory classes throughout the trimester for on campus students. This requirement is stipulated by the Australian Social Work Education and Accreditation Standards (ASWEAS). This is an approved Student Income Support course. Eligible students may apply for Youth Allowance or Austudy. Due to a course quota , admission to this course under Rule C and Rule D is subject to closing without notice if the quota is met.

This requirement is met via attendance at the mandatory intensive schools associated with some of the core units for online students and/or via face-to-face mandatory classes throughout the trimester for on campus students. This requirement is stipulated by the Australian Social Work Education and Accreditation Standards (ASWEAS). This is an approved Student Income Support course. Eligible students may apply for Youth Allowance or Austudy. Due to a course quota , admission to this course under Rule C and Rule D is subject to closing without notice if the quota is met.
duration: 2 Years Full-time; Up to 6 years Part-time

faculty: Faculty of Humanities, Arts, Social Sciences and Education
courseName: Master of Strategic Leadership in Risk and Emergency Management
description: The Master of Strategic Leadership in Risk and Emergency Management course is an advanced level course that equips graduates with the skill sets needed in the field. The course is designed by industry for industry to provide critical, analytical and strategic leadership skills for future and mid to senior-level managers within a diverse portfolio of agencies including, but not limited to, private and public security organisations, policing, border security, intelligence organisations, community corrections, military and emergency services. The course focuses on building greater organisational capabilities by skilling managerial staff to provide strategic leadership within global and local environments. These lifelong learning opportunities and transferrable skills enable students to achieve career goals and fortify their career resilience. This course has been designed with three different pathways in mind. The Emergency Management program gives a highly advanced skillset and knowledge for the area of interest and provides a full pathway meeting the needs of the industry and is predominantly taught by staff with executive experience in large agencies. The Legal and Policy pathway ties in the Risk and Emergency Management area within a legal framework and is designed for students who already have a law qualification. The research pathway is designed for students who wish to do further study at a doctoral level as well as gain the full set of skills in the Risk and Emergency Management area.

faculty: Faculty of Humanities, Arts, Social Sciences and Education
description: The Master of Teaching (Primary) is a two-year graduate entry initial teacher education program for pre-service primary teachers. The program is informed by the latest research and contains (i) an introduction to the profession, Aboriginal education, teaching students who have English as an additional language or dialect, teaching and learning, inclusive and special education, classroom behaviour management, literacy and numeracy education and ICT across the curriculum; (ii) nine curriculum methods units; and (iii) 60 days of professional experience are spread across three units in the course, including an 'online demonstration school'. Students are also introduced to research principles and methods and complete a research project as part of their candidature. All students complete a AITSL National Primary Specialisation in English/Literacy . This is an approved Student Income Support course. Eligible students may apply for Youth Allowance or Austudy.

description: The Master of Teaching (Secondary) is a two-year graduate entry initial teacher education program for pre-service secondary school teachers. Candidates may complete up to three designated teaching areas based on their background studies from the following: English, Mathematics, Investigating Science, Agriculture, Biology, Business Studies/Commerce, Chemistry, Computing, Drama, Economics/Commerce, Earth and Environmental Science, Geography, History, Languages, Legal Studies, Mathematics/Physics, Music, Physics, Society and Culture and Studies of Religion. Furthermore, it should be noted that candidates should abide by the letter of offer in terms of their teaching areas. Candidates may also choose the Master of Teaching (Secondary) to take advantage of the Teaching English as an Additional Language or Dialect (EAL/D) specialisation and/or the extended curriculum programs in English, Mathematics, Science and Music. Sixty days of professional experience are spread across three units in the course, including an 'online demonstration school'. Students are also introduced to research principles and methods and complete a research project as part of their candidature. This is an approved Student Income Support course. faculty: Faculty of Humanities, Arts, Social Sciences and Education
courseName: Master of Urban and Regional Planning
description: The Master of Urban and Regional Planning offers a comprehensive grounding in urban and regional planning. The course is fully accredited with the Planning Institute of Australia and graduates are eligible for membership of the Institute's Urban and Regional Planning Chapter. We have a diverse range of admission pathways. If you have a bachelor's degree or higher, you will be eligible for admission to the MURP. Depending on your admission pathway, the MURP can be completed via coursework alone, or coursework and a major research project. As part of your studies, you will be working on real-world planning projects in collaboration with industry partners. At UNE, online study is about flexibility and support that can only be provided by a university that has long understood the challenges faced by adults balancing work, family/life and study. We have three teaching periods (trimesters), commencing in February, June and October, giving you greater choice about when and how much you study each year. The MURP can be completed in a faster timeframe than any comparable Australian planning degree.
duration: 1.5 Years Full-time; Up to 6 years Part-time

description: Most units offered at UNE are available to eligible students on a Non-Award basis. Students undertaking units on a Non-Award basis should refer to the ' Domestic Non-Award Fees ' webpage for unit costs. To find suitable units you may wish to refer to the Program of Study (which lists relevant units) found on the Course Rules and Plans tab of each course in the Course and Unit Catalogue, or search for individual units in the Units section of the Course and Unit Catalogue. The unit information in the Course and Unit Catalogue includes: unit description, where and when the unit is offered, pre-requisites and co-requisites (required background knowledge to study the unit), intensive school information (whether the unit has a mandatory or non-mandatory intensive school which requires attendance), textbook information and unit coordinator details. Most units are offered at 6 credit points [this is equivalent to .125 eftsl (equivalent full-time student load) and equivalent to 150 hours of total student workload]. These units can be taken to enhance and enrich your knowledge and may be counted towards a course at UNE or elsewhere, subject to course rules.

faculty: Learning and Teaching Transformation
description: Available to on-campus International students only. The Postgraduate International Qualifying Program is a non-award program for students who have not met the requirements for admission to a specified Masters degree at UNE. Upon successful completion of this course, you will have the necessary skills to succeed in postgraduate-level studies. The program will provide you with a pathway to one of the following courses: Master of Business Administration (International) Master of Cybersecurity and Computing Master of Information Technology Master of Science in Agriculture. The Postgraduate International Qualifying Program will also allow you to concurrently undertake one academic unit from the specified Master’s degree and receive credit towards that course. The Postgraduate International Qualifying Program is only delivered full-time, on-campus in Armidale. You can apply for this program if you have completed, at minimum; a THREE Year post-secondary qualification in your home country; OR a Bachelor qualification from a recognised university that is comparable to an Associate Degree under the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF).

faculty: Graduate Research School
description: The Professional Doctorate includes structured research training (24 credit points of postgraduate coursework) and a research thesis (168 credit points) designed for experienced professionals to contribute to the development of original knowledge via research-integrated professional practice. The coursework and practice-based research project equip doctoral graduates to lead professional practice while advancing scholarly knowledge and inquiry within their professional contexts. Workplace based research projects are jointly developed by UNE and professional partners, with research internships strongly encouraged. Eligible Australian and New Zealand students who meet the criteria for entry to the Professional Doctorate may not incur tuition fees and may be funded under the Australian Government's Research Training Program (RTP) for the duration of the course. International Students incur tuition fees.

faculty: Faculty of Humanities, Arts, Social Sciences and Education
description: TRACKS Indigenous Foundation Program is a tertiary program for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students who would like to develop the necessary skills and knowledge to undertake undergraduate studies at UNE. The program offers flexible learning and first-hand experience in university study. It has been developed to provide students with an opportunity to access and explore tertiary education and to make informed choices about the future direction of their education. You will be able to draw upon your own experiences and values while developing skills needed to be successful in tertiary education. Completion of TRACKS can help you to meet the eligibility requirements for the Miroma Bunbilla Program, which is a pre-entry pathway for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants to the Joint Medical Program. Eligible domestic students are exempt from the student contribution amount for HECS. Targeted Tutorial Assistance (TTA) is available for students enrolled in the TRACKS program. Please contact the Oorala Aboriginal Centre for all enquiries related to the program.
duration: 1 Year Full-time; Up to 4 years Part-time
